characterList.description: The Lab Assistant is a Caucasian male with a mustache and goatee. He wears glasses and is dressed in a white lab coat over a blue shirt.
characterList.name: Lab Assistant

content_metadata.description: A guided experiment video focusing on chemical equilibrium and spectrophotometry.

qAndA.answer: Experiments Q1 and Q2 are designed to study chemical equilibrium, particularly the equilibrium between iron 2+ ions and ligands.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of experiments Q1 and Q2?

qAndA.answer: Iron and thiocyanate form a blood-red complex.
qAndA.question: What color complex is formed with iron and thiocyanate?

qAndA.answer: A Spectronic 20 spectrophotometer is used to measure the absorbance of the colored complex, which is related to its concentration.
qAndA.question: What equipment is used to monitor the concentration of the colored complex?

qAndA.answer: The lab assistant demonstrates the use of burettes and pipettes for accurate dispensing of the solutions.
qAndA.question: What types of volumetric glassware are used for dispensing solutions?

qAndA.answer: The solutions used in the experiment can be safely disposed of down the sink with plenty of running water.
qAndA.question: How are the solutions disposed of after the experiment?

narrativeProgression.description: The Lab Assistant introduces experiments Q1 and Q2, which are about chemical equilibrium with iron 2+ ions.
He proceeds to explain that both experiments involve making up multiple solutions of iron and a ligand.

scenes.thematicElements: The experiments focus on chemical equilibrium, specifically the equilibrium between iron 2+ ions and ligands.
scenes.title: Introduction of Experiments

narrativeProgression.description: The video displays an image showcasing different solutions of iron and thiocyanate.
The image transitions to show solutions of iron and phenanthroline.
The Lab Assistant continues explaining the procedure, mentioning the use of spectrophotometry to determine the position of the chemical equilibrium.
He indicates the need to make up about 20 solutions of varying concentrations of iron and ligand.
He points to some volumetric flasks as examples of the containers used for the solutions.

scenes.thematicElements: The Lab Assistant explains that spectrophotometry will be used to monitor the concentration of the colored complex formed in the reaction.
scenes.title: Introduction to Spectrophotometry

activities.description: demonstrating the use of a Spectronic 20
placing a colored solution in the sample compartment

narrativeProgression.description: The Lab Assistant moves to demonstrate the use of a Spectronic 20, pointing out its key features.
He explains how to set the wavelength and prepare the sample compartment.
He then shows how to adjust the transmittance using a blank solution and set the absorbance to zero.
Finally, he demonstrates how to place a colored solution into the Spectronic 20 and take an absorbance reading.

scenes.thematicElements: This scene provides a detailed demonstration of the Spectronic 20, a common spectrophotometer used in chemistry labs.
scenes.title: Demonstrating the Use of Spectronic 20

He concludes by summarizing the steps involved in performing experiments Q1 and Q2, which investigate the equilibrium between iron and various ligands.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This video is to help you with experiments Q1 and Q2, which are about chemical equilibrium.
In both cases they are equilibrium with iron 2 plus ions.
Q1, you are using phyosionate, which makes a blood-red complex with iron.
In Q2 you will be using ortho-finanthrolene, which makes an orange complex.
You've actually used iron ortho-finanthrolene before.
In both cases what you are going to be doing is making up multiple solutions.
I've just got a few small flasks here, but you'll be making up about 20 solutions of
different concentrations of iron plus the ligand.
In some cases you will be holding the concentration of the ligand constant and varying in the concentration
of iron.
In other cases you'll be doing the opposite, holding the iron constant and changing the
concentration of the ligand.
By observing the concentration of the colored complex you will be able to determine the
position of the chemical equilibrium, which is iron plus ligand on one side going to
colored complex on the other side.
You will in all cases be monitoring how much of the colored ligand you have produced
using a spec 20.
You have used a spectronic 20 before, so I'll just give you a quick review.
The machine is here and you turn it on with a left hand knob here.
The first thing you're going to do is set it to the appropriate wavelength.
I'm going to use whoops going the wrong way here.
509 is exactly what I want.
Now the sample compartment is here and if you listen, when there is nothing in there there
is a shutter in the light path, so there is zero light getting as far as the detector.
With this in transmittance mode I adjust this so that I have got 0% of the transmission
of the light being transmitted to the detector.
Now I need to tell it what 100% is.
So I have another key event and remember they've got quite disks on them on a white line.
You line the white line up at the front, put it all the way in and at this point you switch
to absorbance mode and you want to use the right hand knob to set this to zero.
You can also do this in transmittance mode and set it to 100% transmittance.
That's the same thing.
There we have it.
Now in transmittance mode that's going to start flashing.
We've got zero transmittance and with a blank in there it's drifted.
Oops going the wrong way.
One of my difficulties here is that I'm doing this with a freshly switched on instrument.
It's a good idea to turn them on and let them sit for about 10 minutes before you start
taking readings.
You'll then have a QVET of your colored solution, pop it in and that has an absorbance of
0.176 in this particular case.
You will be reading about 20 different solutions.
Once you've got them all ready to go it'll be quite quick.
So I would take this, dump it out, take my solution, rinse it with the next solution to
be measured, dump that as well, fill it again with the second solution, pop it back in and
read.
